source: Written by Claude (claude-opus-5-5) from the county counts (AP via The New York Times), the 2024 baseline and Census ACS 2023 context.

08095.t: In the U.S. Senate race between Hickenlooper and Baisley, Phillips County stayed firmly Republican, giving Baisley 1,376 votes to Hickenlooper's 435, a margin of about 50 points. In 2024 Trump carried it by 63, so the county moved 13 points toward the Democrats. That is slightly more than the typical Colorado county (+12) and slightly less than the state as a whole (+14). It ranks 20th of 64 counties by move. Similar counties moved by varying amounts: Lincoln by 12, Moffat by 13 and Rio Blanco by 5. Turnout was 81% of the 2024 vote, 1,900 ballots against 2,354, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

08061.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Kiowa County gave Baisley 592 votes to Hickenlooper's 87, a Republican margin of 72 points on 700 votes cast. That is a 2-point move toward the Democrats from Trump's 74-point margin over Harris in 2024. Every Colorado county moved left, but Kiowa moved the least of all 64. The typical county shifted 12 points, and the state as a whole shifted 14 as Hickenlooper won by 25. Nearby counties with similar 2024 margins moved much further: Cheyenne 9 points, Washington 10 and Baca 9.

Turnout was 81 percent of the 2024 vote, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

08125.t:
In the U.S. Senate race between Hickenlooper and Baisley, Yuma County stayed heavily Republican but moved 11 points toward the Democrats. Trump carried it by 65 points in 2024; Baisley won it by 54, 2,788 votes to 768. That shift was close to the typical Colorado county's move of about 12 points, ranking 39th of 64, and a little smaller than the state's 14-point swing. Similar counties moved by varying amounts: Lincoln 12, Moffat 13 and Rio Blanco 5.

Turnout fell to 3,721 votes, 80% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

08045.t: In the U.S. Senate race, Garfield County gave Democrat Hickenlooper a 17-point margin over Republican Baisley, 14,189 votes to 9,864. In 2024 Harris carried it by 2 points, so the county moved 15 points toward the Democrats, slightly more than Colorado's 14-point shift and well above the typical Colorado county's 12. It ranks 11th of 64 counties by move. About 25,047 votes were cast, 82% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Among similar counties, Grand moved 10 points, Pueblo 16 and Saguache 18. Every Colorado county moved left.

08041.t:
El Paso County, the largest in Colorado by votes cast, flipped in the U.S. Senate race. Trump carried it by 10 points in 2024; Hickenlooper won it over Baisley by 4, 155,453 to 143,607. That is a 14-point move toward the Democrats, matching the statewide shift and ahead of the typical Colorado county's 12. It ranks 18th of 64 counties, all of which moved left. Among similar counties, Douglas moved 11 points, Pueblo 16 and Weld 18.

Turnout was 82% of the 2024 vote, 313,166 ballots against 380,813, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

08037.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Eagle County backed Democrat Hickenlooper over Republican Baisley by 38 points, 15,549 votes to 6,772. Harris carried the county by 24 points in 2024, so it moved 13 points toward the Democrats. That is slightly less than Colorado's statewide shift of 14 points but a bit more than the typical Colorado county's 12. Eagle ranks 19th of 64 counties by move, and every county in the state moved left. Similar counties moved by comparable amounts: Routt 11 points, Broomfield 12, La Plata 12.

Turnout was 23,161 votes, 83% of the 2024 total. With that many fewer voters, the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

08027.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Custer County went for Baisley over Hickenlooper by 31 points, 2,015 votes to 1,038, out of 3,151 cast. That is 5 points less Republican than its 36-point margin for Trump over Harris in 2024. Every Colorado county shifted toward the Democrats, but Custer's move was the second smallest of the state's 64, well short of the typical county's 12 points, the statewide 14 and the national 14. Comparable counties moved further: Bent 8 points, Teller 9 and Delta 11.

Turnout was 81% of the 2024 vote, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

08059.t:
Jefferson County backed Hickenlooper over Baisley in the U.S. Senate race by 32 points, 196,104 votes to 96,235, up from Harris's 20-point margin over Trump in 2024. That 13-point move toward the Democrats is a little larger than the typical Colorado county's 12 points but a little smaller than the state's 14-point swing and the typical national move of 14. All 64 Colorado counties moved left. Jefferson ranks 23rd by size of move and second by votes cast.

Turnout was 308,515 votes, 85% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Comparable counties moved by similar amounts: Larimer shifted 13 points, La Plata 12 and Arapahoe 16.

08087.t:
Morgan County moved about 19 points toward the Democrats in the U.S. Senate race. Baisley carried it over Hickenlooper 6,422 to 3,346, a 30-point margin, down from Trump's 49-point win in 2024. That was the fourth-largest shift among Colorado's 64 counties, all of which moved left by a typical 12 points, and larger than the state's own 14-point swing. Similar Republican counties moved less: Elbert by 9, Logan by 11 and Prowers by 14.

Turnout fell sharply, with 10,231 votes cast against 13,458 in 2024, about 76% of that total. The count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

08117.t:
Summit County backed Hickenlooper over Baisley in the U.S. Senate race by 51 points, 10,671 to 3,271, up from Harris's 37-point margin in 2024. That 14-point move toward the Democrats is a little larger than the typical Colorado county's 12 points and matches the national typical move of 14. All 64 of the state's counties moved left. Comparable counties moved by similar amounts: Pitkin, Gunnison and Routt each shifted 11 to 13 points.

Turnout fell noticeably. The county cast 14,574 votes, 83% of its 2024 total, so the count cannot tell how much of the shift came from voters changing their minds and how much from differences in who turned out.

08065.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Lake County gave Hickenlooper a 33-point margin over Baisley, 2,120 votes to 1,029 out of 3,340 cast. In 2024 Harris carried it by 16 points, so the county moved 16 points toward the Democrats. That ranks seventh of Colorado's 64 counties, all of which moved left. The typical county moved 12 points, and the state moved 14.

About 85% as many people voted as in 2024, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Among similar counties, Lake moved further than Clear Creek (13 points) and Gilpin (8) but less than Costilla (22).

08043.t:
Fremont County stayed firmly Republican in the U.S. Senate race but moved about 10 points toward the Democrats. Baisley carried it 12,335 to 6,725 over Hickenlooper, a margin of R+28, compared with Trump's R+38 in 2024. That shift was a little smaller than Colorado's statewide swing of 14 points and smaller than the typical county in the state, which moved 12. Fremont ranks 44th of 64 by size of move. Similar counties moved by comparable amounts: Delta and Montrose by 11 points and Teller by 9.

About 19,840 votes were cast, 78% of the 2024 total. With that many fewer voters, the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

08103.t:
Rio Blanco County stayed firmly Republican in the U.S. Senate race, giving Baisley 2,272 votes to Hickenlooper's 555, a margin of 59 points. That is 5 points less Republican than Trump's 64-point margin here in 2024. Every Colorado county moved toward the Democrats, but Rio Blanco moved less than all but two of the state's 64. The typical county shifted 11 points, and the state as a whole moved 14. Similar counties moved roughly twice as far: Lincoln and Yuma by 11 points and Phillips by 13.

Turnout was 2,933 votes, 79% of the 2024 total. With that many fewer voters, the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

08069.t:
In the U.S. Senate race between Hickenlooper and Baisley, Larimer County voted for the Democrat by 30 points, 121,724 to 62,768, up from Harris's 18-point margin in 2024. That is a move of about 13 points toward the Democrats, slightly larger than the typical Colorado county's 12 points and a little smaller than the statewide shift of 14. Every county in the state moved left. Larimer ranks 24th of 64 by size of move and seventh by votes cast.

About 193,582 votes were counted, 86% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Comparable counties moved similarly: Jefferson 13 points, La Plata 12, and Arapahoe 16.

08101.t:
Pueblo County swung from a Trump win to a Hickenlooper win in Colorado's U.S. Senate race. Harris lost it by 5 points in 2024; this time Hickenlooper beat Baisley by 11, 36,434 votes to 29,001, a 16-point move toward the Democrats. That is larger than the statewide shift of 14 points and the typical Colorado county's 12, and it ranks ninth of the state's 64 counties, all of which moved left. Pueblo is one of eight that flipped. It moved further than Douglas and El Paso, which also flipped, and slightly further than Garfield.

About 68,092 votes were cast, roughly 80% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

08009.t:
Baca County stayed heavily Republican in the U.S. Senate race but moved toward the Democrats. Baisley beat Hickenlooper 1,217 to 269, a margin of 62 points, down from Trump's 70-point margin in 2024. That 9-point shift was smaller than in most of Colorado, where every one of 64 counties moved left and the typical county moved 12 points. Baca ranks 53rd by size of move. Similar rural counties moved about the same: Kit Carson 9 points, Washington 10, and Lincoln 12.

Turnout fell sharply, with 1,539 votes cast against 2,004 in 2024, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

08039.t:
Elbert County stayed solidly Republican in the U.S. Senate race, giving Baisley 11,710 votes to Hickenlooper's 4,443, a margin of 42 points. That is 9 points closer than Trump's 51-point win here in 2024. Every Colorado county moved toward the Democrats, but Elbert moved less than most, ranking 54th of 64, against a typical state shift of 12 points and a statewide swing of 14. Similar Republican counties moved further: Morgan by 19 points, Prowers by 14 and Logan by 11.

About 17,128 votes were cast, 84% of the 2024 total. With that many fewer voters, the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

08115.t:
In the U.S. Senate race between Hickenlooper and Baisley, Sedgwick County stayed strongly Republican but by a smaller margin than in 2024. Baisley led 744 to 267, a 45-point margin, down from Trump's 56-point win over Harris. That 12-point shift toward the Democrats matches the typical Colorado county, where all 64 moved left. It is smaller than the statewide move of 14 points and the typical national move of 14.

Voters cast 1,065 ballots, 78% of the 2024 total. Because turnout fell, the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Among similar counties, Logan moved 11 points, Jackson 9 and Dolores 6.

08121.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Washington County stayed heavily Republican but moved about 10 points toward the Democrats. Baisley led Hickenlooper 1,794 to 342, a margin of R+65, down from Trump's R+75 in 2024. Turnout fell to 2,223 votes, 79% of the 2,806 cast two years earlier, so the count cannot tell whether voters changed their minds or some simply stayed home.

All 64 Colorado counties moved left. Washington's shift was slightly smaller than the typical county's 12 points and well below the state's 14-point swing toward Hickenlooper, who won statewide by 25. Among similar rural Republican counties, it moved more than Kiowa (2 points) and about as much as Baca (9) and Cheyenne (9).

08071.t:
Las Animas County went narrowly for Hickenlooper over Baisley in the 2026 Senate race, 3,166 to 3,099, a margin of about 1 point, after backing Trump by 14 points in 2024. Its 14-point move toward the Democrats matched the statewide shift and topped the typical Colorado county's 12 points, ranking 13th of 64. Every county in the state moved left, and this was one of eight to flip from Trump to the Democrat. Similar counties varied: Archuleta moved 15 points and also flipped narrowly, Alamosa moved 20 and Park 10.

Turnout was 6,504 votes, 83% of the 7,792 cast in 2024, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

08077.t: Mesa County stayed Republican in the U.S. Senate race but by much less than in 2024. Baisley led Hickenlooper 40,744 to 32,220, a margin of about 11 points, down from Trump's 24-point win here. That 13-point shift toward the Democrats is slightly larger than the typical Colorado county's 12 points, ranking 21st of 64 in a state where every county moved left. It trails the 14-point national typical move and Weld County's 18-point swing, but exceeds Montezuma and Otero. Turnout fell to 75,999 votes, 83% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell how much of the shift came from voters changing their minds and how much from Republican voters staying home.

08049.t:
Grand County flipped in the U.S. Senate race. Trump carried it by 1 point in 2024; this time Hickenlooper beat Baisley 4,504 to 3,692, a 9-point Democratic margin and a 10-point move toward the Democrats. It was one of eight Colorado counties to go from a Trump win to a Democratic one.

Still, its shift was smaller than most. Every Colorado county moved left, and Grand ranks 43rd of 64. The typical county in the state moved 12 points, the state as a whole 14, and the typical county nationwide 14. Similar counties moved further: Huerfano 14 points, Garfield 15, Saguache 18. The county cast 8,661 votes, 88% of its 2024 total, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

08109.t:
Saguache County moved 18 points toward the Democrats in the U.S. Senate race, going from a 4-point Harris margin in 2024 to a 22-point win for Hickenlooper over Baisley, 1,617 votes to 1,013. That was the fifth-largest move among Colorado's 64 counties, all of which moved left, and bigger than the state's 14-point shift and the typical Colorado county's 12. Comparable counties moved less: Grand by 10 points, Gilpin by 8 and Garfield by 15.

Turnout fell to 2,743 votes, 81% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

08011.t:
Bent County voted for Mark Baisley (R) over John Hickenlooper (D) in the U.S. Senate race by 31 points, 1,040 to 534, out of 1,633 votes cast. That is 8 points closer for the Democrats than Donald Trump's 39-point win over Kamala Harris here in 2024. Every Colorado county moved left, but Bent moved less than most, ranking 55th of 64. The typical county moved 12 points, and the state moved 14. Nearby counties of similar size and lean were mixed: Crowley moved 8 points, Custer 5 and Fremont 10.

Only 75% as many people voted as in 2024, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

08113.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, San Miguel County gave Democrat Hickenlooper 3,110 votes to Republican Baisley's 811, a margin of about 57 points. That is 7 points more Democratic than Harris's 49-point margin here in 2024. Every one of Colorado's 64 counties moved left, but San Miguel's shift ranks 60th, well below the typical county's 12 points and the state's overall 14. Similar counties moved further: Pitkin by 13, Summit by 14 and Boulder by 9.

About 4,062 votes were cast, 85% of the 2024 total. With turnout that much lower, the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

08053.t:
Hinsdale County, the smallest county in Colorado by votes cast, stayed Republican in the U.S. Senate race but by less than in 2024. Baisley won 252 votes to Hickenlooper's 228, a margin of 5 points, down from Trump's 12-point lead over Harris. That 8-point move toward the Democrats ranks 57th of 64 Colorado counties, all of which moved left. The typical county moved 12 points, and the state moved 14 as Hickenlooper won by 25.

Turnout was 83% of the 2024 vote, 500 ballots against 606, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Similar counties moved further: Mineral 11 points, Las Animas 15, and Alamosa 20.

08017.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Cheyenne County gave Republican Baisley 685 votes to Democrat Hickenlooper's 112, a margin of 69 points. That is about 9 points less Republican than its 78-point margin for Trump over Harris in 2024. Every Colorado county moved left. This one moved somewhat less than the typical county's 12 points, ranking 48th of 64, while the state as a whole moved 14 points toward Hickenlooper. Similar counties varied: Washington moved 10 points and Baca 9, while Kiowa moved only 2.

Only 836 votes were cast, 79% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. With 93% of the expected vote counted, the numbers may still move.

08047.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Gilpin County voted for Hickenlooper over Baisley by 20 points, 1,939 to 1,252, out of 3,390 votes counted. In 2024 it backed Harris over Trump by 13 points on 4,129 votes, so the county moved 8 points toward the Democrats.

Every one of Colorado's 64 counties moved left, but Gilpin moved less than most, ranking 58th. The typical county shifted 12 points and the state as a whole 14. Similar counties moved further: Lake by 16 points, Clear Creek by 13 and Costilla by 22. Turnout was 82% of the 2024 vote, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

08079.t:
Mineral County stayed Republican in the U.S. Senate race, but by far less than in 2024. Baisley edged Hickenlooper 311 to 299, a margin of 2 points, after Trump carried the county by 13. That is a shift of about 11 points toward the Democrats, almost exactly the typical move among Colorado's counties, all 64 of which moved left. The state as a whole shifted 14 points. Similar counties split: Hinsdale moved 8 points and stayed Republican, while Las Animas and Archuleta each moved about 15 and narrowly flipped to the Democrats.

Only 642 votes were cast, 85% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell how much of the shift came from voters changing their minds and how much from who stayed home.

08019.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Clear Creek County voted for Hickenlooper over Baisley by 29 points, 3,141 to 1,667. That is up from Harris's 17-point margin over Trump in 2024, a shift of about 13 points toward the Democrats. The county moved slightly less than Colorado as a whole (14 points) and the national typical county (14), and a little more than the typical Colorado county (12), ranking 28th of 64.

Turnout fell to 5,071 votes, 83% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Among similar counties, Lake moved 16 points, Gilpin 8 and Costilla 22.

08025.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Crowley County stayed firmly Republican but less so than in 2024. Baisley beat Hickenlooper 888 to 363, a margin of 40 points, compared with Trump's 47-point win here. That is an 8-point move toward the Democrats, smaller than the typical Colorado county's 12 points and the statewide shift of 14. Every county in the state moved left, and Crowley ranks 56th of 64. Among similar counties, Dolores moved 6 points and Prowers 14.

Only 1,318 votes were cast, 77% of the 1,706 cast in 2024. With that drop, the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

08021.t:
Conejos County stayed Republican in the U.S. Senate race but by much less. Baisley carried it over Hickenlooper 1,765 to 1,597, a margin of 5 points, down from Trump's 18-point win over Harris in 2024. That 13-point shift toward the Democrats is a little larger than the typical Colorado county's 12 points, where all 64 counties moved left, and a little smaller than the national norm of 14. Nearby comparisons split. Park moved 10 points, while Archuleta and Rio Grande each moved about 15.

About 3,458 votes were cast, 84% of the 2024 total. With that drop in turnout, the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

08055.t:
Huerfano County flipped. Trump carried it by 9 points in 2024; in the U.S. Senate race, Hickenlooper beat Baisley here by 5, 1,889 votes to 1,698. That is a 14-point move toward the Democrats, about the same as Colorado's statewide shift and a little more than the typical county in the state, which moved 12. Huerfano ranks 15th of 64 counties by move and is one of eight in Colorado to go from Trump to the Democrat.

Turnout was 3,748 votes, 84% of the 2024 total of 4,438, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Among comparable counties, Las Animas and Archuleta each moved 15 points and Alamosa 20, making Huerfano's swing slightly smaller than theirs.

08001.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Adams County swung harder toward the Democrats than any other Colorado county. Harris carried it by 9 points in 2024; Hickenlooper beat Baisley here by 32, with 124,325 votes to 61,768, a move of 23 points. All 64 of the state's counties moved left, the typical one by about 12 points and the state as a whole by 14. Comparable large counties moved less: Arapahoe by 16 points, Jefferson and Larimer by 13 each.

Voters cast 195,886 ballots, 84% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell how much of the swing came from people changing their minds and how much from people who stayed home.

08023.t:
Costilla County swung hard toward the Democrats in the U.S. Senate race. Hickenlooper beat Baisley 1,223 to 557, a 36-point margin, up from Harris's 15-point edge over Trump in 2024. That 22-point move ranks second among Colorado's 64 counties, all of which moved left. It is nearly double the typical Colorado county's 12 points and well above the national typical move of 14.

Comparable counties moved less: Lake by 16 points, Clear Creek by 13 and Gilpin by 8. Turnout was 1,840 votes, 88% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

08097.t:
In the U.S. Senate race between Hickenlooper and Baisley, Pitkin County voted Democratic by 57 points, 7,012 to 1,850. That is a 13-point move toward the Democrats from Harris's 44-point margin in 2024. Every one of Colorado's 64 counties moved left, and Pitkin ranks 26th. Its shift is slightly larger than the typical Colorado county's 12 points but smaller than the statewide move of 14.

Turnout fell to 9,080 votes, 81% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Among comparable counties, Summit moved 14 points, Gunnison 13 and San Miguel 7.

08035.t:
Douglas County flipped in the U.S. Senate race, going from a 7-point Trump win in 2024 to a 4-point win for Hickenlooper over Baisley, 102,585 votes to 94,118. That 11-point shift toward the Democrats is close to the typical Colorado county's move of about 12 points, and every county in the state moved left. It was a smaller swing than in comparable counties: El Paso moved 14 points, Pueblo 16 and Weld 18. Statewide, the race moved 14 points from 2024.

About 206,030 votes were cast, 85% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. With 98% of the expected vote counted, the result is nearly complete.

08099.t:
Prowers County stayed firmly Republican in the U.S. Senate race, though by less than in the 2024 presidential vote. Baisley beat Hickenlooper 2,649 to 1,181, a 37-point margin, down from a 51-point Republican margin in 2024. That 14-point move toward the Democrats was a little larger than the typical Colorado county's 12 points and close to the state's own 14-point shift, ranking 16th of 64 counties.

Turnout fell to 77% of the 2024 level, with 3,966 votes cast against 5,144, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Among similar counties, Morgan moved further, by 19 points, while Elbert (9) and Dolores (6) moved less.

08051.t:
In the U.S. Senate race between Hickenlooper and Baisley, Gunnison County voted 6,462 to 2,534 for the Democrat, a margin of 42 points. That is 13 points more Democratic than its 29-point margin for Harris over Trump in 2024. The county's shift was slightly larger than the typical Colorado county's 12 points but a little smaller than the statewide move of 14. Every one of Colorado's 64 counties moved left. Similar counties moved by comparable amounts: Routt by 11, Broomfield by 12 and Eagle by 13.

Turnout was 9,377 votes, 86% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

08073.t:
Lincoln County stayed firmly Republican in the U.S. Senate race but by less than in 2024. Baisley beat Hickenlooper 1,416 to 392, a margin of 53 points, down from Trump's 65-point margin over Harris. That 12-point shift toward the Democrats sits at the middle of Colorado, where all 64 counties moved left and the typical county moved by the same amount. It is a little below the national typical move of 14 points.

About 1,934 votes were cast, three-quarters of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Among similar counties, Phillips moved 13 points, Yuma 11 and Rio Blanco 5.

08014.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Broomfield County gave Democrat Hickenlooper 27,412 votes to Republican Baisley's 10,945, a margin of 41 points. Harris carried it by 29 points in 2024, so the county moved 12 points toward the Democrats. That is a little less than Colorado's 14-point statewide shift and the typical national move of 14. All 64 Colorado counties moved left. Broomfield ranked 30th, in the middle, and moved about as much as similar counties such as Routt, Eagle and Gunnison, each of which shifted 11 to 13 points.

Voters cast 40,313 ballots, 86% of the 46,817 cast in 2024, so the count cannot separate people who changed their minds from people who stayed home.

08075.t:
Logan County stayed solidly Republican in the U.S. Senate race but moved about 11 points toward the Democrats. Baisley beat Hickenlooper 5,493 to 1,935, a margin of about 46 points, down from Trump's 57-point win in 2024. That shift almost exactly matches the typical Colorado county, where the middle move was 12 points left and all 64 counties moved left. It also matches similar places nearby: Sedgwick moved 12 points, Moffat 13 and Elbert 9.

Turnout fell sharply. The county cast 7,795 votes, 77% of its 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

08123.t:
Weld County stayed Republican in the U.S. Senate race but by far less than in 2024. Baisley won 72,479 votes to Hickenlooper's 68,040, a margin of 3 points, after Trump carried the county by 21. That 18-point move toward the Democrats ranks sixth of Colorado's 64 counties, all of which moved left, and beats both the typical state move of about 12 points and the national figure of about 14. Comparable counties shifted less: Mesa by 13, Montezuma by 11 and El Paso by 14.

About 148,041 votes were cast, 82% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

08119.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Teller County stayed firmly Republican, backing Baisley over Hickenlooper 8,407 to 4,766, a margin of 27 points. That is 9 points closer than Trump's 35-point win over Harris in 2024. Every one of Colorado's 64 counties moved toward the Democrats, but Teller moved less than most, ranking 51st. The typical Colorado county shifted 12 points, and the typical county nationally shifted 14. Similar counties moved a little more: Delta 11 points, Fremont 10 and Montrose 11.

About 13,677 votes were cast, 84% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

08005.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Arapahoe County gave Hickenlooper 170,691 votes to Baisley's 76,364, a Democratic margin of 36 points, up from Harris's 20-point margin in 2024. That 16-point move toward the Democrats was larger than the state's 14-point shift and ranks eighth among Colorado's 64 counties, all of which moved left. The typical Colorado county moved 12 points. Jefferson and Larimer, counties of similar size and 2024 lean, each moved about 13.

Turnout fell. The 259,598 votes cast were about 80% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

08003.t:
Alamosa County swung hard toward the Democrats in the U.S. Senate race between Hickenlooper and Baisley. Trump carried it by 11 points in 2024; this time Hickenlooper won it by 9, 3,195 votes to 2,639, a move of 20 points. That ranks third among Colorado's 64 counties, all of which moved left, against a typical county move of 12 points and a statewide shift of 14. It is one of eight Colorado counties that went from a Trump win to a Democratic win.

Similar counties moved less: Las Animas, Archuleta and Huerfano each shifted about 14 to 15 points. Alamosa cast 6,085 votes, 81% of its 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

08105.t:
Rio Grande County stayed Republican in the U.S. Senate race but by far less than in 2024. Baisley led Hickenlooper 2,517 to 2,136, a margin of about 8 points, down from Trump's 23-point win. That is a 15-point move toward the Democrats, ranking 10th of Colorado's 64 counties and a little more than the state's 14-point shift. Similar counties moved less: Otero by 10, Montezuma by 11 and Conejos by 13.

Turnout fell sharply, with 4,856 votes cast against 6,194 in 2024, or 78% of the earlier total. The count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Every Colorado county moved left, the typical one by about 12 points, and the typical county nationally by 14.

08015.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Chaffee County voted for Hickenlooper over Baisley by 25 points, 7,752 votes to 4,540. That is a 12-point move toward the Democrats from Harris's 14-point margin in 2024. Turnout was 12,769 votes, 89% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

The county's shift matched Colorado's typical county move of 12 points and fell just short of the statewide move of 14. Every Colorado county moved left. Among similar counties, Chaffee moved more than Gilpin (8 points) and less than Clear Creek (13) and Lake (16).

08089.t:
Otero County stayed Republican in the U.S. Senate race but by less than in 2024. Baisley won 3,964 votes to 2,808 for Hickenlooper, a margin of 16 points, down from Trump's 26-point win here. That is a 10-point move toward the Democrats, slightly smaller than the typical Colorado county's 12 points and the state's 14. Every county in Colorado moved left; Otero ranks 46th of 64.

Turnout fell to 7,033 votes, 79% of the 2024 total of 8,925, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Comparable counties moved similarly or further: Montezuma and Montrose by 11 points each, Rio Grande by 15.

08085.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Montrose County stayed Republican but by less than in 2024. Baisley led Hickenlooper 12,423 to 7,942, a margin of 21 points, down from Trump's 33-point win over Harris. That is an 11-point move toward the Democrats, a little smaller than the state's 14-point shift and close to the typical Colorado county. All 64 counties in the state moved left. Similar Republican counties moved about as much: Delta by 11 points, Fremont by 10 and Teller by 9.

About 21,022 votes were cast, 82% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

08007.t:
Archuleta County voted narrowly for Hickenlooper over Baisley in the U.S. Senate race, 3,405 to 3,363, a Democratic margin of about 1 point. Trump carried it by 14 points in 2024, so the county moved about 15 points toward the Democrats. That is a little more than Colorado's typical county (+12) and close to the state's 14-point shift. It was one of eight Colorado counties to flip from Trump to the Democrat. Las Animas, which started from a similar margin, made almost the same move.

Only 6,999 votes were cast, about 75% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. With 94% of the expected vote counted, the numbers may still move.

08013.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Boulder County gave Democrat Hickenlooper 135,191 votes to Republican Baisley's 26,373, a 65-point margin, up from Harris's 56-point margin in 2024. That is a 9-point move toward the Democrats, smaller than the state's 14-point shift and the typical Colorado county's 12. Every Colorado county moved left, and Boulder ranks 53rd of 64 by size of move.

About 168,613 votes were cast, 86% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Among similar counties, Denver, which started at nearly the same 2024 margin, moved 14 points, Pitkin moved 13, and San Miguel moved 7.

08033.t:
Dolores County stayed firmly Republican in the U.S. Senate race, giving Baisley 866 votes to Hickenlooper's 298, a margin of 47 points. That is 6 points less Republican than Trump's 53-point margin in 2024. Every Colorado county moved toward the Democrats, but Dolores moved less than most, ranking 61st of 64. The typical county moved 12 points, the state 14, and the nation 14.

Similar small, heavily Republican counties moved further: Sedgwick 12 points, Jackson 9, and Crowley 8. Turnout was 1,202 votes, 85% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell how much of the shift came from voters changing their minds and how much from those who stayed home.

08111.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, San Juan County backed Hickenlooper over Baisley 392 to 150, a Democratic margin of 43 points on 568 votes. That is 11 points more Democratic than Harris's 32-point margin over Trump in 2024. The shift is close to the typical Colorado county's move of about 12 points and short of the statewide swing of 14. Every county in the state moved left. San Juan ranks 42nd of 64 by size of move and 63rd by votes cast.

Turnout reached 97% of the 2024 vote. Similar counties moved by comparable amounts: Gunnison 13 points, Routt 11 and Ouray 8. With about 94% of the expected vote counted, these numbers may still move.

08031.t:
Denver County gave Hickenlooper, the Democrat, a 70-point margin over Republican Baisley in the U.S. Senate race, 254,474 votes to 39,286, with 99% of the expected vote counted. Harris had carried the county by 56 points in 2024, so it moved 14 points toward the Democrats. That is almost exactly the statewide shift and the typical national move.

The move ranks 14th among Colorado's 64 counties, all of which moved left. The typical one shifted 12 points. Boulder, which was similarly Democratic in 2024, moved 9 points, and Pitkin moved 13. Denver cast 305,655 votes, 84% of its 2024 total, so the count cannot tell how much of the shift came from voters changing their minds and how much from who stayed home.

08057.t:
Jackson County stayed firmly Republican in the U.S. Senate race but moved 9 points toward the Democrats. Baisley won 455 votes to Hickenlooper's 158, a margin of 46 points, down from Trump's 55-point margin in 2024. That shift was smaller than Colorado's typical county move of 12 points and the statewide move of 14, and it ranks 49th of 64 counties. Among similarly sized Republican counties, Sedgwick moved 12 points, Crowley 8 and Dolores 6.

Only 645 votes were cast, 77% of the 2024 total and the fourth-smallest count in the state. With turnout down that much, the count cannot tell whether voters changed their minds or some simply stayed home.

08029.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Delta County stayed firmly Republican but moved 11 points toward the Democrats. Baisley carried it 9,802 to 5,786 over Hickenlooper, a margin of 25 points, down from Trump's 36-point win in 2024. That shift is close to Colorado's typical county move of 12 points, in a state where all 64 counties moved left. Delta ranks 41st by size of move. Similar counties moved by comparable amounts: Teller by 9 points, Fremont by 10 and Montrose by 11.

About 16,214 votes were cast, 83% of the 2024 total. With that drop in turnout, the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

08093.t:
Park County stayed Republican in the U.S. Senate race, but by much less than in 2024. Baisley beat Hickenlooper 4,823 to 4,215, a margin of 6 points, after Trump carried the county by 17. That is a 10-point move toward the Democrats, slightly smaller than the typical Colorado county's 12 and the statewide shift of 14. It ranks 45th of 64 Colorado counties by move, and every county in the state moved left.

Turnout was 9,484 votes, 79% of the 12,044 cast in 2024, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Similar counties moved further: Archuleta and Las Animas each shifted 15 points and flipped to narrow Democratic wins, and Conejos moved 13.

08067.t:
La Plata County moved about 12 points toward the Democrats in the U.S. Senate race, where Hickenlooper beat Baisley here 19,273 to 9,917, a margin of 31 points. In 2024 Harris carried the county by 19. About 30,113 votes were cast, roughly 84% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

The shift was close to the norm. Every one of Colorado's 64 counties moved left, the typical one by about 12 points, and La Plata ranked 29th. Similar counties moved by similar amounts: Eagle 13 points, Larimer 13 and Chaffee 12. Statewide the move was 14 points, the same as the typical county nationally.

08063.t:
Kit Carson County stayed solidly Republican in the U.S. Senate race but moved toward the Democrats. Baisley beat Hickenlooper 2,269 to 533, a margin of 60 points, down from Trump's 68-point win in 2024. That shift of about 9 points was smaller than in most of Colorado, where every county moved left and the typical one moved 12. Kit Carson ranked 52nd of 64. Statewide, Hickenlooper won by 25 points, a 14-point move from 2024.

Turnout fell sharply: 2,918 votes were cast, 79% of the 2024 total of 3,698. The count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Among similar counties, Baca also moved 9 points, Yuma 11 and Rio Blanco 5.

08091.t:
Ouray County moved toward the Democrats in the U.S. Senate race, but by less than most of Colorado. Hickenlooper beat Baisley here by 29 points, 2,224 to 1,210, up from Harris's 21-point margin in 2024, a shift of 8 points. Every one of the state's 64 counties moved left, and the typical one moved 12 points. Ouray ranks 59th by size of move. Among similar counties, it matched Gilpin (8 points) and trailed Clear Creek (13) and Lake (16).

Turnout was 3,538 votes, 86% of the 2024 total. With that drop, the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

08083.t:
In the U.S. Senate race between Hickenlooper and Baisley, Montezuma County stayed Republican but by much less than in 2024. Baisley carried it 6,685 to 5,447, a margin of about 10 points, down from Trump's 21-point win over Harris. That is a shift of 11 points toward the Democrats, almost exactly the typical move among Colorado counties, all 64 of which moved left, and a bit smaller than the state's 14-point swing.

Turnout fell: 12,559 votes were cast, 83% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Similar counties moved about as much, with Park and Otero each shifting 10 points and Rio Grande 15.

08081.t:
In Colorado's U.S. Senate race, Moffat County stayed firmly Republican but moved toward the Democrats. Baisley led Hickenlooper 3,616 to 1,117, a margin of R+50, compared with Trump's R+63 in 2024. That is a 13-point shift left, slightly smaller than the statewide move of 14 points and a little larger than the typical Colorado county's 12. Every county in the state moved left. Nearby counties with similar 2024 results ranged from Rio Blanco's 5-point move to Phillips's 13.

Only 4,977 votes have been counted, 75% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. With about 92% of the expected vote in, the numbers may still move.

08107.t:
In the U.S. Senate race between Hickenlooper and Baisley, Routt County gave Hickenlooper 9,250 votes to Baisley's 3,889, a margin of 39 points. That is 11 points more Democratic than its 28-point margin for Harris over Trump in 2024. The shift was close to the typical Colorado county's 12-point move, and a little smaller than the state's 14-point swing and the national typical move of 14. Similar counties moved slightly more: Gunnison and Eagle by 13 points each, and Broomfield by 12.

Turnout was 13,690, or 84% of the 2024 vote. With that many fewer ballots, the count cannot tell how much of the move came from voters changing their minds and how much from who stayed home.
